event_summary: 1917年、63歳のヤナーチェクは38歳年下の人妻カミラ・ストッスロヴァーと出会い、以降11年間で700通以上の手紙を送り続けた。この一途な想いが晩年の弦楽四重奏曲など数々の傑作を生む創作源になった。
sources: https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/レオシュ・ヤナーチェク
https://ja.wikipedia.org/wiki/弦楽四重奏曲第2番_(ヤナーチェク)
hook_copy: 63歳、[G]38歳年下の人妻[/G]への手紙700通が傑作生んだ
portrait_prompt: Oil-painting style illustrated portrait of Czech composer Leoš Janáček in his later years (around age 63-70, early 20th century), bust-to-shoulder composition. He has a distinctive bald head with closely cropped white hair remaining only at the sides and back, a broad rounded weathered face, deep-set thoughtful eyes, and a full, bushy white/grey mustache and short white goatee beard covering his chin, giving him a stern yet dignified expression. He wears a dark early-1900s formal suit jacket with a high white stiff collar and a dark cravat or necktie, in the simple, sober style typical of a Moravian gentleman of his era, no gold embroidery or decorative flourishes. Skin has a weathered, ruddy Central European complexion. Illustrated cinematic style, painterly rendering, not photorealistic. Plain, muted solid-color background (soft dark neutral tone) with no vignette, no border, no frame edge, artwork extending fully to all four edges of the canvas with no margin. No text anywhere in the image.

middle_slides.text: 1917年夏、63歳のヤナーチェクは、38歳も年下ですでに結婚していたカミラという女性と出会い、たちまち心を奪われてしまう。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustrated scene set in summer 1917 at a spa resort garden in Moravia. An elderly composer in his sixties with a bald head, white hair at the sides, a bushy white mustache and short white goatee, wearing a dark early-1900s suit with a white stiff collar, stands facing forward among leafy trees and garden paths, his face lit with sudden captivated wonder as he gazes toward an elegant young woman in a pale early-1900s dress walking nearby, seen from the side in a sunlit garden path. Warm golden summer light, painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text anywhere.

middle_slides.text: 以降、ヤナーチェクは亡くなるまでの11年間、カミラに宛てて700通以上もの手紙を書き続けた。その想いは晩年まで冷めることはなかった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustrated scene of the same bald elderly composer with white mustache and goatee, dark early-1900s suit, sitting at a wooden writing desk by candlelight or window light, deeply absorbed in writing a letter with a quill or fountain pen, stacks of many handwritten letters and envelopes piled beside him on the desk, warm sepia-toned interior lighting, his expression tender and wistful, seen from a three-quarter front angle so his face is visible while he writes. Painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text anywhere.

middle_slides.text: この一途な想いこそが晩年の創作意欲の源となり、弦楽四重奏曲「ないしょの手紙」をはじめ、数々の傑作を生み出す原動力になった。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustrated scene of the same bald elderly composer with white mustache and goatee, dark early-1900s suit, seated at a piano in a study filled with music manuscript paper, composing with great passion and energy, one hand on the keys and the other gesturing as if inspired, sheet music and scattered pages around him, warm dramatic lighting suggesting late-night creative fervor, face turned toward the viewer with an intense inspired expression. Painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text anywhere.

middle_slides.text: 70歳を目前にした1923年、弦楽四重奏曲「クロイツェル・ソナタ」は、彼女への想いのままにわずか9日間で書き上げられた。
middle_slides.image_prompt: Oil-painting style illustrated scene of the same bald elderly composer, now nearing seventy, with white mustache and goatee, dark early-1900s suit, working feverishly at a cluttered writing desk covered in music manuscript pages, candle burning low beside him, his face shown in three-quarter view with an urgent, feverish concentration as if racing against time to finish a composition, papers slightly scattered from rapid writing, dim warm interior lighting emphasizing intensity and urgency. Painterly brushwork, not photorealistic, no text anywhere.

fb_caption:
1917年夏、モラヴィアで63歳の作曲家は、38歳も年下ですでに人妻だったカミラという女性と出会い、たちまち心を奪われてしまう。ヤナーチェクはその後11年間で700通以上もの手紙を送り続け、それが晩年の傑作群の原動力になった✨

「忙しい大人のためのクラシック音楽ノート」では、忙しい日々の合間に、
ほんの数分だけ立ち止まりたくなる、クラシック音楽の物語を発信しています。
指揮者マエストロ・ノートが案内する、作曲家たちの知られざる人生の
ドラマ——栄光の裏にあった挫折、常識をくつがえす意外な真実——を、
毎日少しずつお届けしています。

難しい知識は必要ありません。ただ、物語として楽しんでいただければ、
それだけで十分です。

他の作曲家の逸話も知りたい方は、チャンネルもチェックしてみてください。https://youtube.com/@classicalmusic_note?si=evg6wej2KOx2uPhH
